findings.title: Repository visibility metadata did not match observed GitHub state

evidence.observation: GitHub reported kanadhiayash/grimoire visibility as public while the baseline REPOSITORY_INDEX.json declared private.
The RED commit reproduced the mismatch as private != public.

findings.close_condition: REPOSITORY_INDEX.json declares public visibility and exact-head checks pass.

findings.title: Active authoritative surfaces retain Zeref-era runtime naming

evidence.reference: AGENTS.md; README.md; REPOSITORY_INDEX.json; policies/; standards/; adapters/; src/; templates/; checks/
evidence.observation: Active current-state surfaces contain Zeref or ZEREF_ runtime references while the intended active runtime boundary is Shiroe.

findings.close_condition: Active v2 policy and output use a runtime-neutral execution contract, Shiroe is isolated behind an adapter, and Zeref remains only in explicit compatibility or historical paths.

findings.title: Normative authoring contract is not enforced corpus-wide

evidence.observation: The authoring contract requires 25 sections for every normative standard, while multiple normative documents do not contain those sections and current checks do not reject them.

findings.close_condition: Every normative record is validated against an explicit record kind and complete machine contract, with human rendering parity enforced.

findings.title: Four supported stack overlays remain migration-required

evidence.observation: Node-TypeScript, Python, React Native-Expo, and SwiftUI-iOS are classified LEGACY_NORMATIVE with review_status MIGRATION_REQUIRED.

findings.close_condition: All four supported stack overlays are migrated to current v2 OVERLAY contracts with supported-version, source, deprecation, verification, and compatibility metadata.

findings.title: Normative source registry lacks adopted official-source records

evidence.observation: Current source records are local_policy records pointing back to local Grimoire standards; no official_source record exists under registry/sources at the baseline commit.

findings.close_condition: Every externally-derived release-blocking requirement maps to verified current official-source records and local policy is clearly distinguished from external authority.

findings.title: Machine contract completeness is optional outside universal governance

evidence.observation: The registry requires the full eight-field contract only for universal-governance; other normative domains can omit contract or provide a partial object.

findings.close_condition: Every normative record kind has a closed required machine contract and incomplete normative records fail validation.

findings.title: Legal-compliance is omitted from the required standard-area check

evidence.observation: REQUIRED_STANDARD_AREAS includes universal, engineering, github, ai-development, product-ux, and stacks but not standards/legal-compliance.

findings.close_condition: Work-type/domain coverage is driven by the canonical work-type registry and all declared supported domains are fail-closed release gates.

findings.title: Evidence-confidence vocabulary is duplicated and inconsistent

evidence.observation: The repository uses overlapping but different evidence labels across normative standards instead of one canonical machine vocabulary.

findings.close_condition: One canonical vocabulary source defines evidence confidence and all policies, schemas, standards, compiler output, and tests consume it without divergent duplicates.

findings.title: Approval action classes are duplicated across policies

evidence.observation: Approval-gated action lists are maintained in more than one policy surface with different breadth.

findings.close_condition: Approval action classes are defined once in canonical vocabularies and referenced by all policies and schemas.

findings.title: Source precedence is repeated across authoritative surfaces

evidence.observation: Authority and source-precedence concepts are encoded in multiple locations, creating drift risk even where current ordering is similar.

findings.close_condition: One canonical precedence model is machine-defined and other surfaces render or reference it without redefining the ordering.

findings.title: Source review cadence is too coarse for fast-changing authority

evidence.observation: Current local source records generally use roughly one-year review expiry regardless of domain volatility.

findings.close_condition: Source records carry risk-sensitive review policy and currentness states, with release-blocking adopted sources required to be CURRENT.

findings.title: Legal source coverage is explicitly non-exhaustive and lacks a temporal applicability engine

evidence.observation: The legal registry declares foundation-not-exhaustive coverage and current applicability logic does not provide a dedicated effective-date and transition-window engine.

findings.close_condition: Official legal sources are current and temporal applicability supports publication, effective dates, transition windows, future-effective requirements, and supersession.

findings.title: Product and UX coverage is foundation-level rather than complete by declared work type

evidence.observation: The capability map describes foundation or planned expansion in product strategy, research, design systems, and related product work instead of executable FULL work-type coverage.

findings.close_condition: Every declared supported product/design work type has a machine work-type record, complete controls, sources, evidence classes, scenarios, and FULL coverage status.

findings.title: Engineering and operations coverage lacks explicit work-type completeness

evidence.observation: Engineering coverage is described by broad foundation standards and does not expose a machine release gate for incident operations, infrastructure/platform overlays, identity, data/ML lifecycle, and other declared 2.0 work types.

findings.close_condition: Every declared supported engineering/operations work type has complete machine coverage and representative verification scenarios.

findings.title: Human normative Markdown and machine records lack universal parity enforcement

evidence.observation: Current corpus checks verify classification and registry mapping but do not universally prove that human normative content is a rendering of the canonical machine contract.

findings.close_condition: Normative Markdown is generated or parity-checked from canonical machine records and drift fails CI.

findings.title: No dedicated cross-standard contradiction engine exists

evidence.observation: The baseline has no dedicated deterministic validation surface for opposing modalities, duplicate requirement ownership, active superseded requirements, or canonical vocabulary contradictions across standards.

findings.close_condition: A deterministic contradiction engine blocks structurally provable conflicts and emits non-provable semantic conflicts for human review.

findings.title: Windows remains outside the verified runtime matrix

evidence.observation: Required runtime jobs cover Ubuntu and macOS, while README explicitly reports Windows as NOT_VERIFIED.

findings.close_condition: Windows is part of the required blocking CI matrix and passes all supported Python jobs on the release candidate.

findings.title: Required Python support matrix ends at 3.13

evidence.observation: The baseline supported contract is Python 3.11, 3.12, and 3.13 only.

findings.close_condition: The approved Grimoire 2.0 Python support matrix includes every required supported version and passes on all required operating systems.

findings.title: Compiled pack lacks a dedicated human-first entrypoint and complete explainability UX

evidence.observation: The baseline pack exposes AI_CONTEXT.md and structured artifacts but does not provide the planned START_HERE.md hierarchy or work-type/source explain commands for progressive human and AI use.

findings.close_condition: Human and AI entrypoints, explainability commands, stable recovery language, and representative journey tests pass.

findings.title: Security policy does not expose a complete supported-version and private-reporting contract

evidence.observation: The policy defines defensive handling expectations but does not provide a complete supported-version table and explicit private vulnerability-reporting contact path.

findings.close_condition: Public security documentation states supported versions and an owner-approved private reporting path without exposing sensitive information.
